against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "For my New Year reset, create a short, practical reset and upkeep guide for the watercolor setup I established at Cherrywood. Use the actual workspace and supplies from that setup. Include initial, per-session, weekly, and occasional upkeep that keeps the area ready for painting.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Cherrywood Watercolor Setup — Reset & Upkeep", "body": "# Cherrywood Watercolor Setup — Reset & Upkeep

A light-touch routine for the naturally lit dining-corner painting table and narrow supply cabinet. Keep the usual supplies together: paints, palettes, brushes, boards, 140-pound cold-press paper, tape, pencils, towels, and two water containers. The goal is a clear, ready-to-use station—not a bigger organizing project.

## Initial New Year reset
- Clear the painting table and palette shelf; wipe them clean and let them dry. Keep a board under the work area to protect the permanent table surface.
- Return paints, palettes, brushes, paper, tape, pencils, towels, and water containers to their usual places in or beside the narrow cabinet. Keep the current paper easy to reach and stored flat and dry.
- Check that brushes are clean and dry, paper is sound, and tape and pencils are usable. Refill only what is actually running low; no duplicate kit is needed.
- Keep the portfolio and finished work out of direct sun. The corner gets strong afternoon light; don’t leave artwork or paper where a sunbeam lands.
- Keep the table orientation that avoids afternoon glare on wet paper. If the light shifts, turn the painting setup/table 90 degrees; use the white foam board on the shadow side if useful.

## Every session
**Before:** Set a board on the table, take out one sheet, palette, brushes, paints, pencil, tape, towels, and two water containers. Put clean and rinse water on the same reachable side so your painting hand doesn’t cross the sheet. Check for direct sun or glare; adjust the angle before starting.

**After:** Let the painting dry flat in a clear, separate spot—don’t stack or cover it while damp. Rinse brushes until clear, reshape the tips, and lay them flat or store them bristles-up only once dry. Empty and rinse both water containers. Wipe the palette’s mixing surface and table/board; leave reusable paint in the palette to dry rather than scrubbing out sound pans. Put tools back together and leave the table clear except for safely drying work.

## Weekly (about 10 minutes)
- Wipe the table and palette shelf; check for dried drips, stray tape, or pencil shavings.
- Check the brush tips and handles, paper stack, and paint supply at a glance. Put paper back flat and dry; keep damp towels and wet work away from stored paper and supplies.
- Clear the drying spot and return fully dry paintings to the portfolio. Check that stored work remains away from direct sunlight.
- Confirm both water containers and the white foam board are clean and ready for the next session.

## Occasionally (monthly or when something changes)
- Clean stubborn dried pigment from palette mixing wells with water and a soft cloth; avoid harsh scraping. Check paint pans/tubes for depletion or damage and replace only what is needed.
- Inspect boards for dried paint or tape residue; clean gently so the next sheet has a clean backing. Test low-tack tape on scrap before using it on a finished sheet, and remove it from fully dry paper at a low angle.
- Recheck the afternoon light and seasonal sun path. Keep wet-paper glare controlled and move the portfolio if direct sun reaches it; don’t put artwork against a hot exterior wall.
- If the area has been unused, do a quick dry-surface check before setting out paper: no standing water, damp cloths, or wet paintings near the supplies.
